newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - April 9.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Sources have revealed that as many as 11 out of the 12 clubs playing under the Australian Rugby League banner are ready to confirm their continued support for the ARL and have privately indicated they will sign loyalty documents committing them to the Opts Cup in 1998. Sydney City is believed to be the only club yet to make a firm commitment. Page 20.

Rachael Downs is currently preparing to head to Europe next month for the first time to gain valuable international experience ahead of next year's world dressage championship in Ireland after sweeping the prize pool at Australia's most prestigious dressage show, the Trivett Classic International Dressage Event in Sydney last weekend. Her performance was so good, one judge said it drew people to tears. Page 20.

In a vote of confidence that runs contrary to reports of dissatisfaction from senior St Kilda players with their coach Stan Alves, the players have pledged their total support for the embattled coach, whose future has been the subject of speculation becaue of the team's poor performance so far this Australian Football League season. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

While the Perth Western Reds announced last night that captain Mark Geyer and his legal counsel, solicitor Chris Murphy, would appeal Geyer's seven-match suspension for an eye gouging incident, Geyer risks having his ban significantly extended when he appars before the Super League appeals committee early next week. Page 46.

Robert Shaw, the former coach of the Adelaide Crows AFL side, has been appointed as an advance scout for the Sydney Swans - a position which will see him providing advance reports on some of the Swans' opponents, as well as being a sounding board for Sydny coach Rodney Eade. Page 46.

Soccer Australia made an outstanding payment of A$25,000 yesterday to seven Socceroos who were owed the amount from winning bonuses earned from international games played in January. The payment came within 24 hours of Soccer Australia chairman David Hill revealing he had learnt of the debt. Page 45.
THE AGE

The Sydney Swans is considering including champion full-forward Tony Lockett, who has been in rehabilitation after groin surgery but is improving quickly, in its line-up for Friday's match against Melbourne at the Sydney Cricket Ground if he trains well tnight. Page B16.

Just two days after having a nine-match suspension for pushing an umpire overturned by the Supreme Court, Carlton footballer Greg Williams be back before the AFL Tribunal tonight after being charged last night with kneeing North Melbourne's Dean Laidley dring Monday's match. Page B16.

Lisa Moro and Zeena McLaughlin, two 15-year-old Australians, beat Olympic gymnastics champion Simona Amanar to come first and second respectively in the all-round event at the Wild Rose invitational competition in Canada. Page B14.
THE HERALD SUN

Following a move by the Australian Football League yesterday to refuse to change the starting time of the Round 4 match against Brisbane on Sunday, from 12.45pm to later in the afternoon due to heat concerns, North Melbourne chief Greg Miller warned the AL it would be accountable for the safety of the club's players if they suffer in the hot conditions. Page 80.

In Brisbane yesterday, cricketing legend Dennis Lillee said Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor, who has not reached 50 in his past 20 Test innings, should not be retained in his position for the upcoming Ashes tour just because of his captaincy skills Page 78.

The West Coast Eagles confirmed yesterday that wingman Chris Mainwaring, described by the club's football manager Trevor Nisbett as one of the team's best five players for the past 10 years, would miss the rest of the AFL season after injuring his knee onSaturday in a match against Geelong. Page 78.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Parramatta rugby league coach Brian Smith has reacted to the club's poor start to the season by dumping Aaron Raper, Troy Campbell and David Woods from first grade and giving 20-year-old rookie hooker Daniel Brown the chance to make his top-grade debut at Parramatta Stadium on Saturday against Manly. Page 80.

A Northern Transvaal player has avoided being cited for a kneeing incident which put New South Wales rugby union prop Andrew Blades in hospital with at least one fractured vertebrae in his back, after New South Wales officials failed to cite the Northern ransvaal player within the required 12 hours. Page 78.

New South Wales Super League captain Laurie Daley has predicted that thanks to the new Super League rules - combined with the traditional inter-State rivalry - Friday night's Tri-series game against Queensland will be the fastest match he has ever played,with both teams having plenty of pace out wide and mobile forwards. Page 77.
